# Benchmark

How well does PubGround ground a biomedical claim in the literature, compared with
widely used open-source retrievers, rerankers and published claim verifiers? Every system is
run in this harness on the same claims, corpus, candidate lists and metrics.

**All tables, with every metric: [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md)** (generated by `make_report.py`).

## Datasets

| Dataset | Claims | Corpus | Evaluates |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SciFact** (BEIR test = SciFact dev) | 300 | 5,183 abstracts | retrieval + verdict |
| **SciFact-Open** | 279 (SciFact test claims; 206 with evidence) | 500,000 S2ORC abstracts | retrieval + verdict at realistic scale |
| **HealthVer** (test split) | 230 COVID health claims, 903 claim–abstract pairs | 322 abstracts | verdict (3-class) |

## Systems

- **PubGround (this project).**
  - Retrieval: BM25, MedCPT dense, Hybrid RRF(BM25, MedCPT dense), the MedCPT cross-encoder
    reranker, and Stage 1 LLM query expansion (the pipeline's own prompt).
  - Verdict: an LLM judge that outputs SUPPORT / CONTRADICT / NEI plus rationale sentences.
  - LLMs: claude-haiku-5.5, deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 and claude-sonnet-5.5 via OpenRouter, and a local Qwen3-8B.
- **Retrieval baselines.** e5-large-v2, bge-large-en-v1.5, SPLADE (SciFact only),
  Qwen3-Embedding-4B, ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12, bge-reranker-v2-m3, monoT5-3B and Qwen3-Reranker-4B.
  Every reranker scores the identical top-100 candidate list.
- **Verdict baselines.**
  - **VeriSci** (the SciFact paper's system), trained on SciFact train.
  - **MultiVerS zero-shot** (`fever_sci` checkpoint), never trained on SciFact or HealthVer.
  - **MultiVerS supervised**: the `scifact` checkpoint, trained on SciFact train+dev, and the `healthver`
    checkpoint, trained on HealthVer train.
  - Train/eval claim overlap was checked for every comparison (see caveats).

The removed Stage 5 (LLM re-verification of reranked matches) is not part of the pipeline or of
this benchmark. An earlier run on SciFact found it improved nDCG@10 by at most +0.007 with API models
(Haiku +0.0068, DeepSeek −0.0004) and lowered it with the local Qwen3-8B (−0.0165).

## Headline results

**Retrieval, nDCG@10**

| | SciFact (5K) | SciFact-Open (500K) |
|---|---|---|
| BM25 | 0.652 | 0.561 |
| Best single first-stage model | 0.784 (Qwen3-Embedding-4B) | 0.699 (bge-large) |
| **Hybrid + MedCPT rerank (PubGround components, no LLM)** | 0.792 | 0.750 |
| PubGround Stage 1 LLM-QE + MedCPT rerank (best LLM) | 0.798 | 0.754 |
| Hybrid + monoT5-3B | 0.770 | 0.778 |
| Hybrid + Qwen3-Reranker-4B | **0.802** | **0.806** |

**Verdict, abstract-level label F1**

| | SciFact oracle | SciFact open | SciFact-Open open | HealthVer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VeriSci | 0.734 | 0.552 | 0.349 | 0.198 |
| MultiVerS zero-shot | 0.631 | 0.552 | 0.314 | 0.307 |
| MultiVerS supervised (in-domain where fair) | contaminated | contaminated | 0.438 | **0.777** |
| **PubGround judge, best of Haiku / DeepSeek / Sonnet** | **0.873** | **0.660** | **0.470** | 0.514 |
| PubGround judge, local Qwen3-8B | 0.711 | 0.419 | 0.350 | 0.618 |

## Findings

1. **Hybrid retrieval is the most robust component.**
   - Fusing BM25 with MedCPT dense raises Recall@100 over BM25 on both corpora (0.873 → 0.973; 0.864 → 0.964).
     It is the best first stage on SciFact-Open; on SciFact, MedCPT dense (0.982) and Qwen3-Embedding-4B (0.977)
     alone are marginally higher.
   - On SciFact it raises every reranker's nDCG@10 by 0.018–0.046 compared with BM25 candidates
     (on SciFact-Open only MedCPT was run on both: +0.031).
2. **MedCPT reranking is competitive on the small corpus but not at 500K scale.**
   - On SciFact it is within 0.010 of Qwen3-Reranker-4B (difference not significant) with ~1/36 of the parameters
     and ~1/18 of the wall-clock time (59 s vs 1,062 s on one H100, single run, including model loading, for the
     40,634 unique pairs in the union of the BM25 and hybrid top-100 lists of the 300 claims). It is above bge-reranker-v2-m3
     (+0.058, 95% CI 0.031–0.087) and MiniLM (+0.100, 0.070–0.131), and marginally above monoT5-3B (+0.022, 0.000–0.043).
   - On SciFact-Open it falls to third (0.750 vs 0.806 for Qwen3-Reranker-4B and 0.778 for monoT5-3B); it no longer
     differs from bge-reranker-v2-m3 (+0.013, −0.021–0.047) and still beats MiniLM (+0.111, 0.077–0.146).
   - MedCPT dense likewise trails general-purpose embedders at scale.
3. **LLM query expansion (Stage 1) adds recall over BM25 but not over hybrid retrieval.**
   - With the MedCPT reranker it matches Hybrid + MedCPT within ±0.01 on both datasets.
   - A local Qwen3-8B is about as good here as API models.
4. **The zero-shot API judges (Haiku, DeepSeek, Sonnet) beat every verifier that was not trained in-domain.**
   Paired bootstrap differences in label F1 (`results_ci.json` → `verdict_paired_label_f1`):
   - SciFact gold abstracts: +0.086 (0.017–0.161), +0.099 (0.031–0.172) and +0.139 (0.077–0.207) over VeriSci, which
     was trained on SciFact; on SciFact-Open, evidence-pair accuracy 0.815–0.874 vs 0.402–0.515.
   - SciFact-Open end to end: no difference from the supervised MultiVerS (+0.019 to +0.032, every interval includes 0).
   - HealthVer: the in-domain supervised MultiVerS wins (+0.158 to +0.317 over the judges, all intervals above 0).
     The API judges' recall (0.35–0.40) is lost almost entirely to NEI answers: they answer NEI on 52–57% of HealthVer
     evidence pairs vs 7–12% of SciFact evidence pairs (`verdict_diagnostics`). HealthVer counts support for one part
     of a multi-part claim as SUPPORT (Sarrouti et al. 2021, §3.3), while the verdict prompt asks for direct support;
     the NEI rates are consistent with that mismatch but do not prove it.
5. **End-to-end precision is the bottleneck.** Sending the top-3 abstracts to the judge gives
   P = 0.555–0.573 on SciFact: related but uncited abstracts get labelled SUPPORT/CONTRADICT.
6. **Small local judges are not reliable end to end.** Qwen3-8B labels SciFact-Open gold evidence well (accuracy 0.865)
   but over-calls SUPPORT/CONTRADICT on retrieved abstracts (open precision 0.295–0.314).

## Caveats

- **Contamination.** The released MultiVerS `scifact` checkpoint was trained on a file containing all
  300 SciFact dev claims; it scores 100% there, so it is excluded on SciFact.
  - It is fair on SciFact-Open, which uses SciFact test claims (1 duplicate claim text).
  - The `healthver` checkpoint has no train/test overlap.
- **Reproduction gaps.**
  - MultiVerS is re-implemented on current transformers (same tokenization, global attention, heads).
    The contaminated 100% and its HealthVer score (0.777) indicate a faithful port.
  - VeriSci scores 0.734 oracle label F1 vs 0.774 reported (dev, bootstrap mean). Recall matches; precision is lower.
    The reason is unresolved: possibly the "latest" released checkpoint differs from the paper's.
- **SciFact-Open labels come from pooling** (4 older systems, including a monoT5-based one).
  Relevant abstracts no pooled system found count as negatives. This lowers every system's precision
  and may favour systems similar to the pooled ones.
- **Uncertainty.** Each system was run once; 95% bootstrap intervals over claims and paired differences are in
  `results_ci.json` (`bootstrap_ci.py`). With 206–300 claims, differences below ~0.02 nDCG@10 are generally not
  significant.
- **Timing.** Reranker times are single-run wall-clock seconds that include model loading, with different batch sizes
  and precisions per model; treat the ratios as indicative.
- **Ties.** Qwen3-Reranker-4B scores (bf16 log-probabilities) saturate, so many candidates tie and keep the hybrid order;
  this changes its nDCG@10 by at most 0.006.
- **BM25.** BM25 on SciFact uses `rank_bm25` (0.652). On SciFact-Open it uses a Lucene-parameter BM25
  (k1=0.9, b=0.4), which gives 0.661 on SciFact vs 0.665 published.
- **LLM settings.** Reasoning is disabled where the endpoint allows it; Sonnet 5.5 requires it.
  Haiku's safety filter refused a few claims (e.g. anthrax dispersal); those calls fall back to claim-only search or NEI.
- **Cost.** All LLM calls cost $10.06 on OpenRouter, $8.39 excluding the removed Stage 5 experiment.
  Sonnet verdicts account for $7.74 of that. Every response is cached in `data/llm_cache/`, so reruns are free.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd benchmark
# data: BEIR SciFact (see run_benchmark.py header), SciFact release (labels + sentences)
mkdir -p data/scifact_raw && curl -sL https://scifact.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/release/latest/data.tar.gz | tar xz -C data/scifact_raw
# SciFact-Open, MultiVerS data/checkpoints, VeriSci checkpoints: URLs in run_extra_datasets.py / run_baselines_verdict.py
echo "OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-..." > .env                 # gitignored

Q=local:/path/to/qwen3-8b
python run_llm_benchmark.py --models anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5,deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
       --verdict-models anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5          # SciFact: LLM stages
python run_llm_benchmark.py --models $Q --out results_llm_qwen3-8b.json
python run_baselines_retrieval.py                             # SciFact: retrievers + rerankers
python run_baselines_verdict.py --llms anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5,deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017,anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5,$Q
for t in encode rerank llm verdict report; do                 # SciFact-Open
  python run_extra_datasets.py --dataset scifact_open --task $t --models ...; done
python run_extra_datasets.py --dataset healthver --task verdict --models ...
python make_report.py                                         # -> RESULTS.md
```

On the IU cluster: `sbatch run_job.slurm "<command>"` (h100-debug, 1 h; every step is cached and resumable).
`run_benchmark.py` is the original key-free SciFact script (BM25 / MedCPT dense / MedCPT rerank).
